title: 2023 AMC 12B Problem 17
statement: Triangle \(ABC\) has side lengths in arithmetic progression, and the smallest side has length \(6.\) If the triangle has an angle of \(120^\circ,\) what is the area of \(ABC?\)

solutions.text:
Let the sides be \(6,\ 6+d,\ 6+2d.\) The \(120^\circ\) angle faces the longest side, so \((6+2d)^2=6^2+(6+d)^2\) \(-2\cdot 6\cdot(6+d)\cos 120^\circ.\) Using \(\cos 120^\circ=-\tfrac12\) gives \(3d^2+6d-72=0,\) so \(d=4\) and the sides are \(6,10,14.\) The area is \(\tfrac12\cdot 6\cdot 10\cdot\sin 120^\circ\) \(=30\cdot\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\) \(=15\sqrt3.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Let the sides be \(6,\ 6+d,\ 6+2d;\) the \(120^\circ\) angle is opposite the longest side
Apply the law of cosines with \(\cos 120^\circ=-\tfrac12\) to find \(d,\) then area \(=\tfrac12ab\sin 120^\circ\)
